news.headline: China's big political meeting could see Xi 'tighten discipline' in party
news.story_lead: Plenums are essentially closed door meetings of the Party's central committee that happen at least once a year - Published 5 hours ago A major political gathering is under way in the Chinese capital, with a closed-door meeting of senior figures that could shape the look of the ruling Communist Party in the years to come. The Fifth Plenum brings together around 300 members of the Central Committee and state media said it would pave the way for a "tightening of discipline" within the Party's ranks. The four-day session that started on Monday will give Xi Jinping an opportunity to further consolidate his grip on power following recent purges.
news.full_article_text: Plenums are essentially closed door meetings of the Party's central committee that happen at least once a year - Published 5 hours ago A major political gathering is under way in the Chinese capital, with a closed-door meeting of senior figures that could shape the look of the ruling Communist Party in the years to come. The Fifth Plenum brings together around 300 members of the Central Committee and state media said it would pave the way for a "tightening of discipline" within the Party's ranks. The four-day session that started on Monday will give Xi Jinping an opportunity to further consolidate his grip on power following recent purges. The normally annual plenums are highly secretive, but a summary of decisions and a more detailed document will be made public after. What is a plenum? They are essentially closed door meetings of the Party's central committee that happen at least once a year. There are usually seven plenums during each five-year Central Committee term and they are watched from afar because they are meant to signal the leadership's priorities. The timing for this year's gathering is important because it is a year away from the next Party Congress, where a new set of priorities is set up and a new central committee appointed. Officially, the Central Committee selects the Party's top leadership but the real processes leading to the selection are kept secret within the Party elite. The next Party Congress will almost certainly reappoint Xi as the country's leader, following the abolition of term limits. What is on the agenda this year? Past plenum sessions have been used to declare Xi as "the core" of the Party, abolish term limits which cleared the way for him to remain in power indefinitely, and elevate his personal philosophy â branded as "Xi Jinping Thought" â to the same level as Chairman Mao. This year's plenum is an opportunity for Xi to dictate strategy in the run up to the Congress, ensuring that views are aligned and delegates loyal. Even the location of the meeting, which will wrap up on Thursday, has not been announced. Past plenums have been held inside Beijing's Jingxi Hotel. According to a readout from the powerful 21-member Politburo this September, the plenum will adopt a decision on "several major issues persistently advancing the comprehensive strict governance of the Party", which is being read as a way to further ensure obedience and effectiveness from distant party officials. This means it would also be a time of nervousness for delegates as they look around the room with its "empty chairs" following the scale of recent purges within the Party. Allegations of corruption, even "moral corruption", have seen large swathes of senior figures culled. "Moral corruption" has been seen by experts as a way of cracking down on perceived disloyalty to Xi because overall disloyalty to the Party can be interpreted as a breach of "morality". The Asia Society Policy Institute has estimated that of 44 military members appointed to the Central Committee in 2022 only two have not been taken down. The all-powerful seven-man Central Military Commission, which runs the armed forces in China, has also been whittled down to only two people, Xi Jinping and one other general. This plenum is an opportunity for him to appoint new officers to this body. news.headline: 'WhatsApp calls, honey-trap': Ex-Army man held in Tamil Nadu for sharing information with suspected Pakistani woman
news.story_lead: 'WhatsApp calls, honey-trap': Ex-Army man held in Tamil Nadu for sharing information with suspected Pakistani woman Investigators said P Babu retired from the army in 2022 after 28 years of service and has since been teaching at the National Cadet Corps academy in Chennai. A 52-year-old retired honorary Indian Army captain from Kannamangalam in Tamil Nadu’s Vellore has been arrested for allegedly sharing information on military activities with a suspected Pakistani woman he met on a social media platform and posed as a Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) research assistant, police said on Monday. Investigators said P Babu retired from the army in 2022 after 28 years of service and has since been teaching at the National Cadet Corps academy in Chennai.
news.full_article_text: 'WhatsApp calls, honey-trap': Ex-Army man held in Tamil Nadu for sharing information with suspected Pakistani woman Investigators said P Babu retired from the army in 2022 after 28 years of service and has since been teaching at the National Cadet Corps academy in Chennai. A 52-year-old retired honorary Indian Army captain from Kannamangalam in Tamil Nadu’s Vellore has been arrested for allegedly sharing information on military activities with a suspected Pakistani woman he met on a social media platform and posed as a Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) research assistant, police said on Monday. Investigators said P Babu retired from the army in 2022 after 28 years of service and has since been teaching at the National Cadet Corps academy in Chennai. They added that Babu allegedly shared information about the purchase and stock of weapons. Also Read | Agra ex-army man awarded life term for killing son Online entrapments of defence personnel The case is the latest in a series of online entrapments of defence personnel. Andhra Pradesh’s Counter Intelligence Cell this month questioned 13 Navy personnel and identified 18 suspects over the alleged sharing of maritime intelligence with Pakistani operatives. A 44-year-old Indian Air Force Wing Commander was arrested in May for allegedly sharing sensitive defence information and classified documents. Also Read | Ex army man sentenced to death for 2014 triple murder in UP’s Aligarh Shared information on WhatsApp, case of ‘honey-trap’ - What investigator said An investigator called Babu’s case a “honey-trap” and said that he allegedly shared information with the woman through WhatsApp. At one stage, Babu asked her why she was asking such details about the Indian Army. She responded, claiming she was with DRDO, the defence ministry’s research and development wing. The woman would call Babu on WhatsApp on the pretext of a DRDO project and seek information on military activities. Babu allegedly shared the information and also requested his former colleagues to do so at the woman’s request. Police said they have seized Babu’s smartphones. They cited initial investigations and said it emerged that he purchased five mobile connections under his name over the last few months to communicate with the woman. Also Read | Panchkula: Trial against army man accused of killing wife begins next month Babu, who was handed over to police after the intelligence agencies interrogated him, was booked under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Sections 152 (endangering India’s sovereignty, unity and integrity) and Section 3 (1)c and 5 (1) (a) of the Official Secrets Act, which relate to the collection, recording or publishing of secret codes or sensitive information prejudicial to India’s security. Babu was produced before a court on Saturday and remanded to the central prison in Vellore.

news.headline: India’s balancing act: Managing border tensions with China and uncertainty with the US
news.story_lead: India’s balancing act: Managing border tensions with China and uncertainty with the US In a conversation on Point Blank, HT's Shishir Gupta discusses India's balancing act with China and the US with Aayesha Varma, stressing strategic autonomy. India’s relations with China and the United States demand different kinds of balance. Along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), the challenge is to hold ground while keeping military and diplomatic channels open.
news.full_article_text: India’s balancing act: Managing border tensions with China and uncertainty with the US In a conversation on Point Blank, HT's Shishir Gupta discusses India's balancing act with China and the US with Aayesha Varma, stressing strategic autonomy. India’s relations with China and the United States demand different kinds of balance. Along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), the challenge is to hold ground while keeping military and diplomatic channels open. With Washington, it is to pursue trade and energy cooperation while preparing for shifts in US policy. In a conversation on Point Blank, Hindustan Times Executive Editor Shishir Gupta discussed these pressures with senior anchor Aayesha Varma, arguing that India’s approach rests on strategic autonomy and a willingness to engage without surrendering its position. Arunachal Pradesh: Tensions, but no immediate sign of escalation The discussion began with remarks by the outgoing chief of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police, who had referred to face-offs at multiple points in Arunachal Pradesh in July. Gupta cautioned against treating a farewell-speech comment as a complete account of the situation. National security, he said, draws on information from military, paramilitary, intelligence and other government institutions; a public statement from one official may not capture the full picture. Gupta described the border situation as a contest between competing claims, with India maintaining that Arunachal Pradesh is an integral part of the country and China claiming the territory. Along the LAC, he said, patrols can enter areas each side considers its own, creating the risk of face-offs. He argued that such incidents do not, by themselves, mean one side has gained control or that a wider confrontation is imminent. According to Gupta, Indian forces had taken countermeasures and established a position intended to provide leverage, while military and diplomatic talks continued at several levels. He said the matter remained unresolved, but that the two sides were holding their positions and there had been no clashes. On that basis, he assessed the likelihood of escalation as very low at the time of the interview. That distinction matters: a standoff can be serious without immediately becoming a conflict. Gupta pointed to the long timelines involved in resolving border disputes, citing the 1986 Sumdorong Chu episode and the continuing efforts to address friction in eastern Ladakh after 2020. His message was that dialogue and a firm military posture can coexist - and that progress on the ground may take time. Also Read: 'India, China continue using existing mechanisms to avoid LAC miscalculations': MEA after ITBP chief's remarks Who ordered the patrols? Several explanations remain possible Varma asked whether the Chinese patrol activity had Beijing’s approval or reflected the initiative of a local commander. Gupta said it was difficult to determine from the information available. He outlined several possibilities rather than presenting one as established fact. One possibility, he suggested, was that local commanders might act more aggressively under pressure to demonstrate performance, particularly amid reported changes and personnel purges in China’s military leadership. Another was that instructions for more assertive patrolling had come from higher up the chain of command. He also pointed to China’s development of border villages and infrastructure, which he said could shape how both sides perceive activity along the frontier. These were Gupta’s interpretations, not confirmed explanations for the reported face-offs. His broader point was that the command picture and motives were uncertain, while military and diplomatic communication remained active. He also said Indian forces were prepared to maintain their positions through winter conditions. Washington: Cooperation alongside unpredictability The conversation then turned to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s visit to India and the status of a potential trade deal, tariffs and Russian oil. Gupta described the visit as constructive, noting discussions on terrorism and the possibility of diesel supplies from Reliance’s Jamnagar refinery. He also said External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar raised India’s concerns about Pakistan. But a positive diplomatic visit, Gupta argued, did not guarantee predictable outcomes. He characterised the trade negotiations as unfinished, saying India was looking for two things: a competitive rate compared with other countries and greater certainty that terms would not change abruptly. The broad parameters might be in place, he said, but the agreement could not be treated as settled until it was signed. Energy added another layer. Gupta said the US was exploring interim diesel supplies from Jamnagar, while a 60-day tariff waiver offered only temporary relief. In his assessment, US decisions were strongly shaped by domestic priorities, including prices and electoral politics. That could make Washington’s policy shifts difficult for partners to anticipate. The contrast with the China discussion is striking. On the border, India’s stated approach is tied to peace and tranquillity: Gupta said relations cannot move forward normally if that condition breaks down. With the US, the relationship is framed more around mutual interests, but trade and energy decisions remain vulnerable to changing political calculations. Also Read: China updates visa application process for Indians, new rules now in effect Strategic autonomy - and more options Gupta described India’s approach as strategic autonomy: cooperating with major powers where interests align, while resisting the idea that it must choose one side. He also linked this stance to India’s ambition to represent the concerns of the Global South and prevent wider-power competition from imposing costs on developing countries. That approach, as presented in the interview, includes broadening India’s options. Gupta pointed to potential energy links with Canada, including Alberta oil, and to a prospective trade agreement with the European Union. Diversifying partners and supply chains, he suggested, could reduce dependence on any single relationship and give India more room to manoeuvre. The interview’s central argument is that India’s balancing act is not simply equidistance between Washington and Beijing. It is a combination of firm positions, selective cooperation and efforts to preserve choices. Along the China border, that means maintaining deployments while pursuing dialogue. With the US, it means seeking trade and energy gains while recognising that policy can change. For Gupta, the common thread is that India must stand its ground - and keep alternative paths open. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Shishir Gupta Shishir Gupta is Executive Editor at Hindustan Times and one of India's top journalists covering national security, strategic affairs, foreign policy and geopolitics. Also Read: 'India, China continue using existing mechanisms to avoid LAC miscalculations': MEA after ITBP chief's remarks Who ordered the patrols? Several explanations remain possible Varma asked whether the Chinese patrol activity had Beijing’s approval or reflected the initiative of a local commander. Gupta said it was difficult to determine from the information available. He outlined several possibilities rather than presenting one as established fact. One possibility, he suggested, was that local commanders might act more aggressively under pressure to demonstrate performance, particularly amid reported changes and personnel purges in China’s military leadership. Another was that instructions for more assertive patrolling had come from higher up the chain of command. He also pointed to China’s development of border villages and infrastructure, which he said could shape how both sides perceive activity along the frontier. These were Gupta’s interpretations, not confirmed explanations for the reported face-offs. His broader point was that the command picture and motives were uncertain, while military and diplomatic communication remained active. He also said Indian forces were prepared to maintain their positions through winter conditions. Washington: Cooperation alongside unpredictability The conversation then turned to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s visit to India and the status of a potential trade deal, tariffs and Russian oil. Gupta described the visit as constructive, noting discussions on terrorism and the possibility of diesel supplies from Reliance’s Jamnagar refinery. He also said External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar raised India’s concerns about Pakistan. But a positive diplomatic visit, Gupta argued, did not guarantee predictable outcomes. He characterised the trade negotiations as unfinished, saying India was looking for two things: a competitive rate compared with other countries and greater certainty that terms would not change abruptly. The broad parameters might be in place, he said, but the agreement could not be treated as settled until it was signed. Energy added another layer. Gupta said the US was exploring interim diesel supplies from Jamnagar, while a 60-day tariff waiver offered only temporary relief. In his assessment, US decisions were strongly shaped by domestic priorities, including prices and electoral politics. That could make Washington’s policy shifts difficult for partners to anticipate. The contrast with the China discussion is striking. On the border, India’s stated approach is tied to peace and tranquillity: Gupta said relations cannot move forward normally if that condition breaks down. With the US, the relationship is framed more around mutual interests, but trade and energy decisions remain vulnerable to changing political calculations. Also Read: China updates visa application process for Indians, new rules now in effect Strategic autonomy - and more options Gupta described India’s approach as strategic autonomy: cooperating with major powers where interests align, while resisting the idea that it must choose one side. He also linked this stance to India’s ambition to represent the concerns of the Global South and prevent wider-power competition from imposing costs on developing countries. That approach, as presented in the interview, includes broadening India’s options. Gupta pointed to potential energy links with Canada, including Alberta oil, and to a prospective trade agreement with the European Union. Diversifying partners and supply chains, he suggested, could reduce dependence on any single relationship and give India more room to manoeuvre. The interview’s central argument is that India’s balancing act is not simply equidistance between Washington and Beijing. It is a combination of firm positions, selective cooperation and efforts to preserve choices. Along the China border, that means maintaining deployments while pursuing dialogue. With the US, it means seeking trade and energy gains while recognising that policy can change. For Gupta, the common thread is that India must stand its ground - and keep alternative paths open. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Shishir Gupta Shishir Gupta is Executive Editor at Hindustan Times and one of India's top journalists covering national security, strategic affairs, foreign policy and geopolitics. news.exam_corner_topic: Cyclone Arnab & Satellite Tracking via INSAT-3DS
static_gk: INSAT-3DS is an advanced meteorological satellite launched by ISRO to provide enhanced weather tracking, atmospheric profiling, and ocean observation capabilities.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD), founded in 1875, operates under the Ministry of Earth Sciences and serves as the primary agency for meteorological observations and tropical cyclone forecasting.
news.headline: Bay of Bengal Cyclone Arnab Intensifies Towards Andhra Pradesh Coast; Tracked by INSAT-3DS Satellite
news.story_lead: India's INSAT-3DS meteorological satellite is actively tracking Cyclone Arnab over the east-central and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the storm is expected to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm before making landfall along the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam on October 28. In response, disaster management authorities in Andhra Pradesh and neighbouring Odisha have initiated high-alert protocols and relief deployments.
news.full_article_text:
### Satellite Monitoring & Storm Coordinates
Data from India's INSAT-3DS weather satellite identified intense convective cloud patterns over the central and southern Bay of Bengal, marking the steady intensification of Cyclone Arnab. In its bulletin issued at 8:30 AM IST on October 26, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) fixed the storm's centre at 15.5°N latitude and 88.8°E longitude. At that time, the system was positioned approximately 610 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 690 km east-southeast of Kakinada, advancing westward at a speed of 15 kmph.

### Intensity Forecast & Landfall Path
- **Intensification Stages**: The IMD forecast indicates that the cyclone will intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by the night of October 26, and further upgrade to a very severe cyclonic storm on October 27.
- **Landfall Target**: The storm is projected to turn northwestward and cross the Andhra Pradesh–Yanam coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by the forenoon of October 28.
- **Wind & Rainfall Parameters**: Sustained wind speeds of 115–125 kmph, with peak gusts reaching 140 kmph, are expected during landfall. Extremely heavy rainfall is predicted in isolated coastal regions.

### Regional Disaster Preparedness & Mitigation
- **Odisha Response**: Although landfall is focused on Andhra Pradesh, Odisha has instituted measures across six vulnerable districts: Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Malkangiri, Koraput, and Nabarangpur.
- **Restrictions**: Fishing operations in the sea and public/tourist access to scenic sites, hills, and waterfalls in these six districts have been banned.
- **Institutional Action**: Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has assigned eight ministers to oversee regional preparedness. State authorities have deployed 24 Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) teams and 6 National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams.
- **Public Safety**: Schools, colleges, and Anganwadi centres in the identified six districts are ordered closed on October 28 and 29. Residents in low-lying areas and thatched structures are being moved to shelters, while pregnant women are being relocated to health facilities.
bullet_points: INSAT-3DS satellite imagery monitored intense convective cloud activity over the east-central and west-central Bay of Bengal.
IMD placed Cyclone Arnab's coordinates at 15.5°N latitude and 88.8°E longitude on the morning of October 26.
The cyclone is forecasted to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm by October 27.
Expected landfall is set between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam along the Andhra Pradesh–Yanam coast by the forenoon of October 28.
Landfall wind speeds are estimated at 115-125 kmph, with gusts reaching up to 140 kmph.
Odisha deployed 24 ODRAF and 6 NDRF teams to handle potential collateral impact in six vulnerable districts.
Fishing activities and tourist visits to vulnerable areas in Odisha's Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Malkangiri, Koraput, and Nabarangpur districts have been prohibited.
Educational institutions and Anganwadi centres across the six identified Odisha districts will remain closed on October 28 and 29.
key_facts: Satellite used: INSAT-3DS
Landfall region: Between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh - Yanam coast)
Forecasted landfall date: October 28 (forenoon)
Maximum sustained wind speed at landfall: 115-125 kmph (gusts up to 140 kmph)
Odisha deployment: 24 ODRAF teams, 6 NDRF teams
Affected Odisha districts: Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Malkangiri, Koraput, Nabarangpur

2026-10-27: Projected intensification into a very severe cyclonic storm.
2026-10-28: Forecasted landfall along Andhra Pradesh coast forenoon.
2026-10-28 to 2026-10-29: Mandatory closure of educational institutions in six vulnerable Odisha districts.
exam_relevance: Prelims: Tropical Cyclones formation in Bay of Bengal, satellite technology in weather forecasting (INSAT-3DS), IMD storm classification, NDRF/ODRAF institutional roles.
Mains (GS III): Disaster Management - Coastal storm mitigation, early warning systems, inter-state disaster response coordination.
news.upsc_analysis: The rapid development of Cyclone Arnab highlights the critical role of modern space technology (such as INSAT-3DS) in providing actionable meteorology for early warnings. Effective coastal disaster mitigation relies on prompt multi-agency coordination between national forecast bodies like IMD and state mitigation agencies such as NDRF and ODRAF, coupled with preemptive administrative steps like evacuations and activity bans.
causes: Vigorous convective activity and favorable atmospheric conditions over the east-central and west-central Bay of Bengal leading to tropical storm intensification.
impacts: Disruption to fishing, maritime, and tourism operations along the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coasts.
Heavy to extremely heavy rainfall threatening localized flooding in coastal districts.
High-speed wind damage (up to 140 kmph gusts) to temporary structures, trees, and power infrastructure in the landfall zone.
challenges: Evacuating populations living in thatched structures and low-lying areas in a short timeframe.
Managing widespread rainfall and wind impacts extending beyond the primary landfall state into neighboring states like Odisha.
government_steps: Deployment of 24 ODRAF teams and 6 NDRF teams across high-risk districts by the Odisha government.
Deputation of 8 state ministers by Odisha CM Mohan Charan Majhi to supervise localized disaster preparedness.
Banning fishing activities and restricting tourist access in Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Malkangiri, Koraput, and Nabarangpur districts.
Pre-emptive transfer of vulnerable individuals, including pregnant women and low-lying residents, to safe shelters and health centres.
constitutional_or_policy_link: Disaster Management Act, 2005 (Framework governing NDRF deployment, state disaster response plans, and executive emergency orders).
way_forward: Strengthen coastal shelter infrastructure and resilient power grid architecture in high-frequency landfall zones.
Ensure real-time integration of INSAT-3DS satellite data with localized emergency alert broadcasting to mitigate loss of life and property.
news.mains_notes:
### Disaster Management & Cyclone Preparedness
- **Role of Satellite Observation**: INSAT-3DS provides real-time tracking of storm coordinates (15.5°N, 88.8°E), cloud convection, and intensity changes over open seas where ground observations are absent.
- **Multi-Agency Action**: Synchronization between IMD forecast bulletins, central forces (NDRF), and state rapid action units (ODRAF) enables targeted early evacuation.
- **Key Interventions**: Proactive bans on coastal/hill activities, relocation of vulnerable groups, and administrative presence (deputing ministers) enhance resilience against extreme weather events.
mains_questions: Examine the role of satellite technology like INSAT-3DS in enhancing tropical cyclone forecasting and disaster risk reduction along India's eastern coast.
Discuss the key challenges in managing coastal cyclone disasters that impact multi-state regions, highlighting institutional mechanisms under the Disaster Management Act, 2005.
news.takeaway: Cyclone Arnab is expected to make landfall between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam on October 28 as a very severe cyclonic storm, tracked by INSAT-3DS and prompting high-level disaster response in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
prelims_facts: INSAT-3DS is India's specialized meteorological satellite used for tracking convective cloud systems and tropical storms.
Cyclone Arnab's forecasted landfall zone is between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam along the Andhra Pradesh–Yanam coastline.
Odisha's six identified vulnerable districts are Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Malkangiri, Koraput, and Nabarangpur.
The expected maximum sustained wind speeds at landfall are 115-125 kmph, with gusts up to 140 kmph.

hindi_translation.headline: बंगाल की खाड़ी में चक्रवात अरनब हुआ तीव्र; आंध्र प्रदेश तट की ओर बढ़ने की INSAT-3DS उपग्रह ने की पुष्टि
hindi_translation.story_lead: भारत का मौसम उपग्रह INSAT-3DS बंगाल की खाड़ी के पूर्व-मध्य और पश्चिम-मध्य क्षेत्र के ऊपर चक्रवात अरनब की लगातार निगरानी कर रहा है। भारत मौसम विज्ञान विभाग (IMD) के अनुसार, इस तूफान के बहुत गंभीर चक्रवाती तूफान में बदलने की संभावना है, जो 28 अक्टूबर को बापटला और विशाखापट्टनम के बीच आंध्र प्रदेश और यनम तट से टकराएगा। इसके जवाब में आंध्र प्रदेश और ओडिशा में आपदा प्रबंधन तंत्र को अलर्ट पर रखा गया है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### उपग्रह निगरानी और चक्रवात की स्थिति
भारत के मौसम उपग्रह INSAT-3DS के आंकड़ों ने बंगाल की खाड़ी के मध्य और दक्षिणी हिस्सों में तीव्र संवहनीय बादलों की गतिविधि की पहचान की है, जो चक्रवात अरनब के मजबूत होने का संकेत है। 26 अक्टूबर को सुबह 8:30 बजे जारी बुलेटिन में IMD ने चक्रवात का केंद्र 15.5°N अक्षांश और 88.8°E देशांतर पर दर्ज किया। उस समय यह तूफान विशाखापट्टनम से लगभग 610 किमी पूर्व-दक्षिणपूर्व और काकीनाडा से 690 किमी पूर्व-दक्षिणपूर्व में 15 किमी प्रति घंटे की गति से पश्चिम की ओर बढ़ रहा था।

### तीव्रता का पूर्वानुमान और लैंडफॉल
- **तीव्रता के चरण**: IMD के अनुसार 26 अक्टूबर की रात तक यह गंभीर चक्रवाती तूफान और 27 अक्टूबर को बहुत गंभीर चक्रवाती तूफान में बदल जाएगा।
- **लैंडफॉल स्थान**: चक्रवात के उत्तर-पश्चिम की ओर मुड़ने और 28 अक्टूबर की दोपहर से पहले बापटला और विशाखापट्टनम के बीच आंध्र प्रदेश-यनम तट को पार करने का अनुमान है।
- **हवा और वर्षा**: लैंडफॉल के दौरान हवा की गति 115-125 किमी प्रति घंटे और झोंके 140 किमी प्रति घंटे तक पहुंचने की संभावना है।

### राज्यों की तैयारी और आपदा प्रबंधन
- **ओडिशा की कार्रवाई**: यद्यपि लैंडफॉल आंध्र प्रदेश में होगा, ओडिशा सरकार ने 6 संवेदनशील जिलों (गंजाम, गजपति, रायगड़ा, मलकानगिरी, कोरापुट और नबरंगपुर) में सुरक्षात्मक कदम उठाए हैं।
- **प्रतिबंध**: समुद्र में मछली पकड़ने और 6 जिलों के पर्यटन स्थलों, पहाड़ियों तथा झरनों पर पर्यटकों के प्रवेश पर रोक लगा दी गई है।
- **संस्थागत कदम**: ओडिशा के मुख्यमंत्री मोहन चरण माझी ने 8 मंत्रियों को तैयारियों की निगरानी का जिम्मा सौंपा है। 24 ODRAF और 6 NDRF टीमें तैनात की गई हैं।
- **जन सुरक्षा**: इन 6 जिलों में 28 और 29 अक्टूबर को स्कूल, कॉलेज और आंगनवाड़ी केंद्र बंद रहेंगे। कच्चे मकानों के निवासियों को सुरक्षित आश्रयों में स्थानांतरित किया जा रहा है।

news.headline: Supreme Court notice to ECI on plea against Maharashtra SIR deletions
news.story_lead: Supreme Court notice to ECI on plea against Maharashtra SIR deletions The Supreme Court posted the matter for hearing on Nov 5, a day before the poll panel is to publish the final state electoral roll after receiving claims and objections. The Supreme Court on Monday sought the response of the Election Commission of India on a petition challenging the special intensive revision (SIR) exercise in the state and an interim direction to keep the process in abeyance till the issue is decided by the court. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant posted the matter for hearing on November 5 after it was informed that the final state electoral roll pursuant to receipt of claims and objections will be published on November 6.
news.full_article_text: Supreme Court notice to ECI on plea against Maharashtra SIR deletions The Supreme Court posted the matter for hearing on Nov 5, a day before the poll panel is to publish the final state electoral roll after receiving claims and objections. The Supreme Court on Monday sought the response of the Election Commission of India on a petition challenging the special intensive revision (SIR) exercise in the state and an interim direction to keep the process in abeyance till the issue is decided by the court. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant posted the matter for hearing on November 5 after it was informed that the final state electoral roll pursuant to receipt of claims and objections will be published on November 6. The petition, filed by Arun Anandagiri, a chartered accountant and journalist, said the situation is so serious that over 40% of the voters in Mumbai and Pune stand deleted. The deletions followed the SIR process with Mumbai recording the highest number of excluded names (around 3.6 million), followed by Pune (2.86 million), Thane (2.85 million) and Nagpur (1.4 million). Senior advocate Arvind Datar appearing for the petitioner said, “The problem faced by Maharashtra is unique. There are 3500 redevelopment projects going on in Mumbai and about 1500 projects in Pune. These persons (displaced by the projects) are to be allotted fresh flats and have been provided alternate accommodations elsewhere. During SIR, they were shown as “not found” in their earlier addresses which has led to their deletion from the rolls. About three crore (30 million) persons have been knocked off the rolls in this manner.” While Datar sought an urgent order to ensure the final roll is not finalised by November 6, the bench, also comprising justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, “Don’t worry. You are a whistleblower. You are before us. We will see if any order is to be passed if the need arises. We will issue orders after hearing the other side.” The court has also sought responses from the Centre, Maharashtra government and the chief electoral officer of Maharashtra on the petition. The matter was mentioned on October 15 for urgent hearing and a request to take up the matter along with the Delhi SIR case. However, Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant said that the issue needs to be dealt with state-wise and that it would hear the matter on October 26. The petitioner stated that he himself has not been excluded from the voter rolls but was alarmed and concerned by such a vast exclusionary exercise. The petition cited news reports to allege flaws in the decision-making process on SIR within the Election Commission of India (ECI) and challenged it on the grounds that decisions taken in this regard were neither unanimous nor taken by majority by the three-member poll panel. To be sure, this is at odds with what has been stated by ECI. The court is already hearing a challenge to the SIR process and the functioning of ECI in a batch of petitions filed by Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and other Opposition leaders. The court is expected to take up these petitions on Tuesday along with pending petitions filed by social activist Rakesh Kumar Singh and advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi . The present petition informed the court that the process for receiving claims and objections from deleted voters in Maharashtra is ongoing as the final electoral roll is slated for publication next month. The petition said that the data is shocking as out of the 97.9 million total voters in the state, about 20 million voters have been deleted and about 12.2 million individuals have been separately flagged for “logical discrepancies”. Datar pointed out that the deleted voters were asked to enrol as new voters by filling Form 6, arguing that this could not be done because these voters would expose themselves to penal consequences by wrongly declaring that they had not voted in any past election. The petition is limited to the SIR challenge in Maharashtra and said that, until the court finally adjudicates the issue, the SIR process for the State of Maharashtra should be kept in abeyance, and no voter whose name appeared in the pre-SIR list should be excluded or deleted. The latest SIR, an electoral roll cleansing drive, started with Bihar in June last year, to remove bogus, duplicate, and ineligible voters, including deceased individuals and “illegal immigrants”. The SIR sparked criticism from the Opposition, which alleged that the exercise is a strategic voter roll clean-up drive by the poll body to benefit the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The SIR in West Bengal was one of the most contentious in recent years, with the deletion of nearly nine million from the electoral roll. The difference in absolute votes the BJP and the Trinamool Congress (TMC) polled was similar to the total SIR deletions. The TMC has maintained that the deletions helped the BJP win West Bengal elections. The BJP, which swept to power in the state for the first time, winning 207 of 294 seats, has rejected this link. - Election Commission Of India

The court is expected to take up these petitions on Tuesday along with pending petitions filed by social activist Rakesh Kumar Singh and advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi . The petition is limited to the SIR challenge in Maharashtra and said that, until the court finally adjudicates the issue, the SIR process for the State of Maharashtra should be kept in abeyance, and no voter whose name appeared in the pre-SIR list should be excluded or deleted. The latest SIR, an electoral roll cleansing drive, started with Bihar in June last year, to remove bogus, duplicate, and ineligible voters, including deceased individuals and “illegal immigrants”. The SIR sparked criticism from the Opposition, which alleged that the exercise is a strategic voter roll clean-up drive by the poll body to benefit the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The SIR in West Bengal was one of the most contentious in recent years, with the deletion of nearly nine million from the electoral roll. The difference in absolute votes the BJP and the Trinamool Congress (TMC) polled was similar to the total SIR deletions. The TMC has maintained that the deletions helped the BJP win West Bengal elections. The BJP, which swept to power in the state for the first time, winning 207 of 294 seats, has rejected this link. - Election Commission Of India

news.headline: Supreme Court issues notice on plea against Chhattisgarh anti-conservation law
news.story_lead: Supreme Court issues notice on plea against Chhattisgarh anti-conservation law Chhattisgarh’s anti-conversion law was the latest in such legislation which rights groups say violates rights The Supreme Court on Monday sought responses from the Union and Chhattisgarh governments in a petition challenging the constitutional validity of Chhattisgarh’s anti-conversion law, directing that it be heard along with pending matters challenging similar laws passed in Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan. In March, the Chhattisgarh assembly passed the law to prevent religious conversions carried out through force, inducement, fraud or misrepresentation. It provides for life imprisonment in cases of mass conversion.
news.full_article_text: Supreme Court issues notice on plea against Chhattisgarh anti-conservation law Chhattisgarh’s anti-conversion law was the latest in such legislation which rights groups say violates rights The Supreme Court on Monday sought responses from the Union and Chhattisgarh governments in a petition challenging the constitutional validity of Chhattisgarh’s anti-conversion law, directing that it be heard along with pending matters challenging similar laws passed in Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan. In March, the Chhattisgarh assembly passed the law to prevent religious conversions carried out through force, inducement, fraud or misrepresentation. It provides for life imprisonment in cases of mass conversion. Chhattisgarh’s anti-conversion law was the latest in a series of such legislation, which civil rights groups say violates an individual’s rights. They are seen as an attempt to curb interfaith marriages. A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notices to the Union and Chhattisgarh governments. Isai Adivasi Mahasabha, an organisation representing tribal Christians, moved the court against the Chhattisgarh legislation. The bench informed the petitioner that a similar challenge is pending before the Chhattisgarh High Court. The bench initially said the matter could be referred to the high court. It added that it would be better if the petitioner pursued the matter in the high court instead of it remaining pending in the Supreme Court. The bench said it is willing to request the high court to expeditiously hear the challenge. Senior advocate Colin Gonsalves, who appeared for the petitioner, noted that similar laws passed are under challenge in the Supreme Court. “Once these matters are decided, the matters before the high court will become redundant.” The bench told Gonsalves it cannot force the petitioners who have approached the high court to come before it. Gonsalves pointed out that he is in touch with the petitioners who filed the case in the high court and that they are of the view the matter ought to have been filed in the Supreme Court. Gonsalves agreed to consult them and consider filing a transfer petition to bring the matters to the Supreme Court. The petitioner said the original version of the Chhattisgarh law was confined to a narrow prohibition against conversion by force, fraud or allurement and did not touch voluntary conversion. It cited the Constitution’s Article 25 (religious freedom) and argued the choice of religious belief is the most intimate expression of personal autonomy of a citizen’s fundamental right. The plea questioned section 2(l)(a) of the Chhattisgarh law, which treats even a promise of a “better lifestyle” as “allurement”. It added that section 2(l)(a)(vii) treats “glorifying one religion against another” as a prohibited inducement. “These formulations are wide enough to capture ordinary religious preaching, exposition of doctrine, and humanitarian or charitable work that this court has repeatedly held to be constitutionally protected,” the petition said. It added that the law exempts “reversion” to ancestral religion or faith even as the expression “ancestral religion” is not defined. The petition challenged the prior declaration under section 4, mandating publication of an applicant’s name for conversion, current faith and proposed religion on the competent authority’s website and on notice boards in the tahsildar office, gram panchayat and local police. Non-compliance with this rule renders the conversion illegal. “This converts the exercise of an inherent fundamental right into a licensed activity, contingent on advance governmental notification and compulsory neighbourhood-level publicity of what this court has repeatedly held to be one of the most private decisions a person can make,” the petition said. The law provides for a fresh post-conversion declaration within 30 days, followed by compulsory personal appearance within 21 days, failing which no Certificate of Conversion shall be issued and the conversion will be rendered “illegal and void”. It provides for a minimum punishment of seven years’ imprisonment. It can extend to 10 years wherever the convert happens to be a minor, a woman, or belonging to the Other Backward Class, Scheduled Caste, or Scheduled Tribe category.

news.headline: Student Movement Unseats Longtime Leader in Serbia's Parliamentary Polls
news.story_lead: In a major political shift, a student-led movement in Serbia has defeated the nation's long-serving leader in parliamentary elections held in October 2026. The election outcome highlights the decisive impact of organized youth mobilization in electoral democracy.
news.full_article_text:
### Electoral Transition in Serbia

In the parliamentary elections conducted in Serbia, a prominent student movement achieved an electoral victory, unseating the long-standing ruling leadership of the country.

* **Electoral Shift:** The election results reported in October 2026 mark a decisive transition in Serbian politics, driven by voter support for student activists against the established government.
* **Role of Mobilization:** Youth organization and civic participation played a primary role in turning out voters and challenging the incumbent regime at the polls.
* **Broader Significance:** The election result reshapes Serbia's domestic governance agenda and carries implications for its political stability and foreign relations.
bullet_points: Serbia held parliamentary elections in October 2026.
A student-led political movement successfully unseated the long-serving incumbent leader.
The election results demonstrate significant political mobilization led by youth activists.
The political transition alters the balance of power in Serbia's national parliament.

* **व्यापक प्रभाव:** चुनाव परिणाम सर्बिया के घरेलू शासन और क्षेत्रीय राजनीतिक समीकरणों को नया रूप दे सकते हैं।

news.headline: Rajasthan: 80 tehsils across 14 districts declared drought-hit
news.story_lead: Rajasthan: 80 tehsils across 14 districts declared drought-hit The districts covered are Banswara, Barmer, Balotra, Bikaner, Churu, Dungarpur, Beawar, Jaisalmer, Jalore, Jodhpur, Phalodi, Nagaur, Pali and Sirohi As many as 80 tehsils across fourteen districts in Rajasthan have been declared drought-affected following deficient rainfall, reduced water availability and damage to the kharif crop. Two notifications issued by the disaster management, relief and civil defence department on October 24 and 25 classify 69 tehsils as severely drought-affected and 11 as moderately affected. The declarations will remain effective for six months from publication.
news.full_article_text: Rajasthan: 80 tehsils across 14 districts declared drought-hit The districts covered are Banswara, Barmer, Balotra, Bikaner, Churu, Dungarpur, Beawar, Jaisalmer, Jalore, Jodhpur, Phalodi, Nagaur, Pali and Sirohi As many as 80 tehsils across fourteen districts in Rajasthan have been declared drought-affected following deficient rainfall, reduced water availability and damage to the kharif crop. Two notifications issued by the disaster management, relief and civil defence department on October 24 and 25 classify 69 tehsils as severely drought-affected and 11 as moderately affected. The declarations will remain effective for six months from publication. The first notification covered 53 tehsils across 13 districts. The second added 27 tehsils across 10 districts, including Bikaner, taking the combined number of affected districts to 14. Of the additional tehsils, 25 have been classified as severely affected and two as moderately affected. The districts covered are Banswara, Barmer, Balotra, Bikaner, Churu, Dungarpur, Beawar, Jaisalmer, Jalore, Jodhpur, Phalodi, Nagaur, Pali and Sirohi. According to the notifications, the assessment considered deficient rainfall, reduced surface and groundwater availability, poor crop conditions and information from the Centre’s Drought Monitoring Portal. The assessment followed the Centre’s Drought Management Manual, 2016. Also Read: Drought-hit Latur bans use of crop residue as industrial fuel Jodhpur has the highest number of affected tehsils at 12, followed by Barmer and Jalore with 10 each, Balotra with nine, Pali with eight, and Dungarpur, Jaisalmer and Phalodi with seven each. Banswara has three, Churu and Beawar have two each, while Bikaner, Nagaur and Sirohi have one each. In Jodhpur, 11 tehsils—Osian, Tinwari, Balesar, Bawri, Shergarh, Sekhala, Kudi Bhagtasni, Jodhpur, Jhanwar, Bilara and Luni—have been classified as severely affected, while Pipar Shahar is moderately affected. All ten listed tehsils in Barmer, Gadra Road, Chohtan, Barmer, Baytoo, Sedwa, Ramsar, Sheo, Dhanau, Barmer Rural and Batadu, are severely affected. Jalore’s 10 tehsils, Ahore, Chitalwana, Jaswantpura, Bagoda, Bhinmal, Raniwara, Sanchore, Sayla, Bhadrajun and Jalore, are also in the severe category. In Balotra, Gudamalani, Kalyanpur, Pachpadra, Gida, Dhorimanna, Patodi, Samdari, Siwana and Sindhari have been classified as severely affected. All eight listed tehsils in Pali—Sumerpur, Desuri, Pali, Bali, Marwar Junction, Rani, Rohat and Sojat—are severely affected. In Jaisalmer, Fatehgarh, Mohangarh, Sam, Ramgarh, Pokaran and Phalsund are severely affected, while Jaisalmer tehsil is moderately affected. In Phalodi, Phalodi, Bap, Bapini, Aau, Ghantiyali and Dechu are in the severe category, while Setrawa is moderately affected. Dungarpur’s Aspur, Galiyakot, Jhauthri and Sabla tehsils have been classified as severely affected, while Simalwara, Paldewal and Obri are moderately affected. In Banswara, Garhi and Arthuna are severely affected and Sajjangarh is moderately affected. Rajgarh and Sidhmukh in Churu, and Sheoganj in Sirohi, have been placed in the severe category. Raipur and Jaitaran in Beawar, Khinvsar in Nagaur and Hada in Bikaner have been classified as moderately affected. Below-normal monsoon According to the Water Resources Department’s report dated September 30 , Rajasthan received 350.83 mm of rainfall between June 1 and September 30 against a normal of 424.71 mm, a shortfall of 73.88 mm. Also Read: Sule seeks ₹ 9,000 aid for farmers, demands ₹ 1L per hectare relief The department classified 14 of the state’s 41 districts as rainfall-deficient, while 24 recorded normal rainfall and three received excess rainfall. The deficient districts included Balotra, Banswara, Dungarpur, Jaisalmer, Jalore, Jodhpur, Pali and Sirohi. The same report recorded water storage in the state’s 693 monitored dams at 62.16% of their combined capacity, compared with 90.19% on the corresponding date last year. In the WRD’s Jodhpur zone, storage stood at just 15.98%, against 80.45% a year earlier.

news.headline: As Kharge's remark sparks row, 'heckler' clarifies 'Modi won't go anywhere' remark
news.story_lead: As Kharge's remark sparks row, 'heckler' clarifies 'Modi won't go anywhere' remark Mallikarjun Kharge's comment sparked a controversy, with BJP leaders accusing him of making “indecent” remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s father. The man who allegedly yelled “Modi won't go anywhere” during Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's address at an event in Bihar has clarified that what he meant was that “as long as there was no rebellion in the country, Narendra Modi won’t go anywhere.” Kharge's reaction to the man's remark was, “Modi ka baap bhi jayega” (Even Modi’s father will go). Speaking at an event to mark the 139th birth anniversary of Shrikrishna Singh, Bihar’s first chief minister, Kharge said the Congress would send those allegedly involved in irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process to jail.
news.full_article_text: As Kharge's remark sparks row, 'heckler' clarifies 'Modi won't go anywhere' remark Mallikarjun Kharge's comment sparked a controversy, with BJP leaders accusing him of making “indecent” remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s father. The man who allegedly yelled “Modi won't go anywhere” during Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's address at an event in Bihar has clarified that what he meant was that “as long as there was no rebellion in the country, Narendra Modi won’t go anywhere.” Kharge's reaction to the man's remark was, “Modi ka baap bhi jayega” (Even Modi’s father will go). Speaking at an event to mark the 139th birth anniversary of Shrikrishna Singh, Bihar’s first chief minister, Kharge said the Congress would send those allegedly involved in irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process to jail. A person in the audience responded by shouting, “Modi won’t go anywhere," drawing the retort from Kharge. Kharge's comment sparked a controversy, with BJP leaders accusing him of making “indecent” remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s father. “Kharge ji’s statement is shameful, sorrowful and utterly condemnable. But what more can one expect from a mafia gang?” the BJP said, demanding that Kharge apologise to the people of the country. Man clarifies remark Speaking to reporters later, the man who made the remark identified himself as Santhosh Kumar, a Congress worker from Chhapra. He claimed that people had mistaken him for a BJP worker because of his intervention during the event. “What I meant was that as long as there is no rebellion in the country, Narendra Modi won’t go anywhere,” he said, news agency PTI reported. BJP demands apology from Kharge What followed Kharge’s remark was criticism and a call for apology from BJP leaders . A BJP worker also filed a police complaint against him over his remarks targeting PM Modi. BJP MP Anurag Thakur said that Kharge must offer an unreserved apology to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the nation for his "indecent" remarks. Speaking to news agency ANI, he said that such statements are testaments to the “ultimate manifestation of the Congress Party’s ideological bankruptcy.” "The influence of Rahul Gandhi’s company is evident in the statements made by Mallikarjun Kharge. Such an indecent remark deserves the strongest possible condemnation. For the national president of the country’s oldest political party to make such an inappropriate comment about the father of the Prime Minister is the ultimate manifestation of the Congress Party’s ideological bankruptcy. The party has become completely devoid of ideology,” he said. “Apologise to the nation. An apology must be offered to Modi ji. The country has now seen the true face of the Congress Party and the state to which it has been reduced today," he added. Home minister Amit Shah said that Kharge has "today torn apart all norms of decorum by making an indecent remark about Modi ji's father in Patna". "This is not the first time that the Congress party has used abusive language against Modi ji or his family. At times, they have hurled insults at his revered mother, at times called him 'merchant of death,' and at times mocked his poverty by calling him 'chaiwala'. "Under Rahul Gandhi's leadership, the Congress party keeps crossing the limits of indecency every day. In the past 12 years, the repeated electoral defeats have bred such desperation and frustration in the Congress party that it no longer has any policy left, nor any issue – only the politics of slander remains," he said in a post on X. Defence minister Rajnath Singh also expressed hurt over Congress president’s remark. In a post on X, Singh said he was “stunned and hurt” by Kharge’s remark made in Patna, Bihar, regarding the Prime Minister’s father. “I am stunned and hurt by the remark made by Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge ji in Patna regarding the revered father of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. Until yesterday, Congress leaders and workers used to mock Prime Minister ji's humble family background and employ indecent language towards his esteemed mother. Today, this same level of base politics has reached the top leadership of the Congress. When a party's top leadership itself forgets the dignity of language, how can one expect decorum from its workers?” Singh said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Karishma Ayaldasani Karishma Ayaldasani is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times, based in New Delhi, where she works with the digital team on fast-moving breaking stories from India and around the world. She enjoys covering national and global news, focusing on delivering updates quickly and clearly so readers can make sense of what’s happening as it unfolds. Comfortable in high-pressure newsroom settings, she regularly contributes to live blogs, explainers and real-time coverage. Before joining Hindustan Times, she was part of the digital team at The Indian Express, worked with the social media team at Firstpost, and spent time as a creative strategist at Clematis Advertising. Outside of work, she likes exploring different art forms and unwinds with music. The man who allegedly yelled “Modi won't go anywhere” during Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's address at an event in Bihar has clarified that what he meant was that “as long as there was no rebellion in the country, Narendra Modi won’t go anywhere.”
Kharge's reaction to the man's remark was, “Modi ka baap bhi jayega” (Even Modi’s father will go).

Speaking at an event to mark the 139th birth anniversary of Shrikrishna Singh, Bihar’s first chief minister, Kharge said the Congress would send those allegedly involved in irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process to jail.
A person in the audience responded by shouting, “Modi won’t go anywhere," drawing the retort from Kharge.

The man who allegedly yelled “Modi won't go anywhere” during Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's address at an event in Bihar has clarified that what he meant was that “as long as there was no rebellion in the country, Narendra Modi won’t go anywhere.” Kharge's reaction to the man's remark was, “Modi ka baap bhi jayega” (Even Modi’s father will go). Speaking at an event to mark the 139th birth anniversary of Shrikrishna Singh, Bihar’s first chief minister, Kharge said the Congress would send those allegedly involved in irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process to jail. A person in the audience responded by shouting, “Modi won’t go anywhere," drawing the retort from Kharge. Kharge's comment sparked a controversy, with BJP leaders accusing him of making “indecent” remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s father. “Kharge ji’s statement is shameful, sorrowful and utterly condemnable. But what more can one expect from a mafia gang?” the BJP said, demanding that Kharge apologise to the people of the country. Man clarifies remark Speaking to reporters later, the man who made the remark identified himself as Santhosh Kumar, a Congress worker from Chhapra. He claimed that people had mistaken him for a BJP worker because of his intervention during the event. “What I meant was that as long as there is no rebellion in the country, Narendra Modi won’t go anywhere,” he said, news agency PTI reported. BJP demands apology from Kharge What followed Kharge’s remark was criticism and a call for apology from BJP leaders . A BJP worker also filed a police complaint against him over his remarks targeting PM Modi. BJP MP Anurag Thakur said that Kharge must offer an unreserved apology to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the nation for his "indecent" remarks. Speaking to news agency ANI, he said that such statements are testaments to the “ultimate manifestation of the Congress Party’s ideological bankruptcy.” "The influence of Rahul Gandhi’s company is evident in the statements made by Mallikarjun Kharge. Such an indecent remark deserves the strongest possible condemnation. For the national president of the country’s oldest political party to make such an inappropriate comment about the father of the Prime Minister is the ultimate manifestation of the Congress Party’s ideological bankruptcy. The party has become completely devoid of ideology,” he said. “Apologise to the nation. An apology must be offered to Modi ji. The country has now seen the true face of the Congress Party and the state to which it has been reduced today," he added. Home minister Amit Shah said that Kharge has "today torn apart all norms of decorum by making an indecent remark about Modi ji's father in Patna". "This is not the first time that the Congress party has used abusive language against Modi ji or his family. At times, they have hurled insults at his revered mother, at times called him 'merchant of death,' and at times mocked his poverty by calling him 'chaiwala'. "Under Rahul Gandhi's leadership, the Congress party keeps crossing the limits of indecency every day. In the past 12 years, the repeated electoral defeats have bred such desperation and frustration in the Congress party that it no longer has any policy left, nor any issue – only the politics of slander remains," he said in a post on X. Defence minister Rajnath Singh also expressed hurt over Congress president’s remark. In a post on X, Singh said he was “stunned and hurt” by Kharge’s remark made in Patna, Bihar, regarding the Prime Minister’s father. “I am stunned and hurt by the remark made by Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge ji in Patna regarding the revered father of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. Until yesterday, Congress leaders and workers used to mock Prime Minister ji's humble family background and employ indecent language towards his esteemed mother. Today, this same level of base politics has reached the top leadership of the Congress. When a party's top leadership itself forgets the dignity of language, how can one expect decorum from its workers?” Singh said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Karishma Ayaldasani Karishma Ayaldasani is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times, based in New Delhi, where she works with the digital team on fast-moving breaking stories from India and around the world. Before joining Hindustan Times, she was part of the digital team at The Indian Express, worked with the social media team at Firstpost, and spent time as a creative strategist at Clematis Advertising. news.headline: 'Indians don't create disturbance on streets': Piyush Goyal's praise for diaspora amid Europe protests
news.story_lead: 'Indians don't create disturbance on streets': Piyush Goyal's praise for diaspora amid Europe protests The minister's comments also come against the backdrop of a protest movement in India against the Election Commission. Union commerce minister Piyush Goyal on Monday stated that the Indian community is a "peace-loving one" and that Indians "do not go on the street and create disturbance to society." Goyal's remarks in Berlin come amid ongoing protests in France, Italy and other parts of Europe. The minister's comments also come against the backdrop of a protest movement in India against the Election Commission.

The minister's comments also come against the backdrop of a protest movement in India against the Election Commission. "Important statistic is, how well you are respected in this country...Good part is you are very wanted, very welcome here. They know you don't indulge in vandalism. They know you don't go on the streets and create disturbance to society, like we are seeing in other parts of Europe. They know that the Indian people and the Indian community are peace-loving. They live with their families, they care for their families," said Goyal, adding that there may be certain exceptions which are "beyond our control." - ABOUT THE AUTHOR HT News Desk Follow the latest breaking news, major developments and agenda-setting stories from India and around the world with the newsdesk at Hindustan Times. news.headline: Pune man gets seven years jail for feeding wife capsules containing blade pieces
news.story_lead: Pune man gets seven years jail for feeding wife capsules containing blade pieces The court also sentenced the accused husband, identified as Somnath Sadhu Sapkal, to three years of rigorous imprisonment for cruelty. A Pune sessions court has sentenced a 45-year-old man to seven years of rigorous imprisonment for attempting to murder his wife by allegedly feeding her capsules containing pieces of a blade under the pretext of giving her medicine. In the October 23 order, which was made available on Monday, the court also sentenced the accused husband, identified as Somnath Sadhu Sapkal, to three years of rigorous imprisonment for cruelty, with both sentences to run concurrently.
news.full_article_text: Pune man gets seven years jail for feeding wife capsules containing blade pieces The court also sentenced the accused husband, identified as Somnath Sadhu Sapkal, to three years of rigorous imprisonment for cruelty. A Pune sessions court has sentenced a 45-year-old man to seven years of rigorous imprisonment for attempting to murder his wife by allegedly feeding her capsules containing pieces of a blade under the pretext of giving her medicine. In the October 23 order, which was made available on Monday, the court also sentenced the accused husband, identified as Somnath Sadhu Sapkal, to three years of rigorous imprisonment for cruelty, with both sentences to run concurrently. Additional Sessions Judge Aniruddha Sulabha Subhash Gandhi convicted the accused under Sections 307 (attempt to murder) and 498A (cruelty by husband or his relatives) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). The court imposed fines of ₹ 50,000 and ₹ 20,000, respectively. The case The case arose from a complaint by Sapkal's wife, Chhaya, who alleged that her husband had been giving her capsules containing blade pieces under the pretext of administering medicine. The incidents reportedly occurred between October 2023 and November 8, 2023. Uttamnagar police registered a first information report on November 14, 2023. According to the prosecution, the woman experienced stomach pain in October 2023 and noticed a piece of a blade passing through her stool. A similar incident occurred later. On November 8, she was taken to hospital with severe abdominal pain. Doctors subsequently removed a blade piece from her stomach through an endoscopic procedure. The prosecution examined seven witnesses, including the complainant, her son, the treating doctor, a medical shop owner, panch witnesses and the investigating officer. Although the complainant and her son did not fully support the prosecution during the trial, the court relied on the medical evidence, the recovery of blade pieces and capsules from the accused's residence, and the testimony of other witnesses. The judge observed that the court had examined the seized articles during the hearing to determine whether the blade pieces could fit inside the capsules. “It was found that the pieces of the blade could be bent and placed inside the capsules. Therefore, it is clearly established that pieces of a blade could be administered to a person through capsules,” the judge observed. The court noted that a medical shop owner, Ganesh Chaudhary, had testified that Sapkal purchased a packet of Almox 500 capsules from him. The prosecution also established that the police had seized the capsule packet and two steel blade pieces from a divan at the accused's residence pursuant to his statement. Medical evidence was central to the court's findings. Dr Poonam Mantri, who treated the complainant, testified that the blade piece found in the woman's stomach posed a threat to her life. The judgement Under the final order, the accused Sapkal was sentenced to seven years of rigorous imprisonment and fined ₹ 50,000 under Section 307. He was also sentenced to three years of rigorous imprisonment and fined ₹ 20,000 under Section 498A. Both sentences will run concurrently. The court also directed that he receive the statutory set-off for the period already spent in custody. Referring to the doctor's testimony, the judge observed, “The pieces of the blade that had entered the complainant's stomach posed a danger to her life, and she could also have died as a result.” The court concluded that administering capsules containing blade pieces amounted to an attempt to murder and constituted cruelty under Section 498A of the IPC. “Feeding capsules containing pieces of a blade to the complainant amounts to an attempt to murder,” the judge held. The court further noted that the accused had allegedly given his wife the capsules over a period of approximately two months and concluded that the prosecution had established the charges under Sections 307 and 498A. However, the court found insufficient evidence to establish the separate allegations that Sapkal had assaulted and abused his wife. It acquitted him of charges under Sections 323 (voluntarily causing hurt) and 504 (intentional insult intended to provoke a breach of peace) of the IPC. During the sentencing hearing, the defence argued that Sapkal was the sole earning member of his family and that his wife was living with him and dependent on him. The court considered these submissions while deciding the punishment. The judge noted the seriousness of the offence but decided against imposing life imprisonment, opting instead for fixed terms of rigorous imprisonment.

hindi_translation.full_article_text: Pune man gets seven years jail for feeding wife capsules containing blade pieces The court also sentenced the accused husband, identified as Somnath Sadhu Sapkal, to three years of rigorous imprisonment for cruelty. A Pune sessions court has sentenced a 45-year-old man to seven years of rigorous imprisonment for attempting to murder his wife by allegedly feeding her capsules containing pieces of a blade under the pretext of giving her medicine. In the October 23 order, which was made available on Monday, the court also sentenced the accused husband, identified as Somnath Sadhu Sapkal, to three years of rigorous imprisonment for cruelty, with both sentences to run concurrently. Additional Sessions Judge Aniruddha Sulabha Subhash Gandhi convicted the accused under Sections 307 (attempt to murder) and 498A (cruelty by husband or his relatives) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). The court imposed fines of ₹ 50,000 and ₹ 20,000, respectively. The case The case arose from a complaint by Sapkal's wife, Chhaya, who alleged that her husband had been giving her capsules containing blade pieces under the pretext of administering medicine. The incidents reportedly occurred between October 2023 and November 8, 2023. Uttamnagar police registered a first information report on November 14, 2023. According to the prosecution, the woman experienced stomach pain in October 2023 and noticed a piece of a blade passing through her stool. A similar incident occurred later. On November 8, she was taken to hospital with severe abdominal pain. Doctors subsequently removed a blade piece from her stomach through an endoscopic procedure. The prosecution examined seven witnesses, including the complainant, her son, the treating doctor, a medical shop owner, panch witnesses and the investigating officer. Although the complainant and her son did not fully support the prosecution during the trial, the court relied on the medical evidence, the recovery of blade pieces and capsules from the accused's residence, and the testimony of other witnesses. The judge observed that the court had examined the seized articles during the hearing to determine whether the blade pieces could fit inside the capsules. “It was found that the pieces of the blade could be bent and placed inside the capsules. Therefore, it is clearly established that pieces of a blade could be administered to a person through capsules,” the judge observed. The court noted that a medical shop owner, Ganesh Chaudhary, had testified that Sapkal purchased a packet of Almox 500 capsules from him. The prosecution also established that the police had seized the capsule packet and two steel blade pieces from a divan at the accused's residence pursuant to his statement. Medical evidence was central to the court's findings. Dr Poonam Mantri, who treated the complainant, testified that the blade piece found in the woman's stomach posed a threat to her life. The judgement Under the final order, the accused Sapkal was sentenced to seven years of rigorous imprisonment and fined ₹ 50,000 under Section 307. He was also sentenced to three years of rigorous imprisonment and fined ₹ 20,000 under Section 498A. Both sentences will run concurrently. The court also directed that he receive the statutory set-off for the period already spent in custody. Referring to the doctor's testimony, the judge observed, “The pieces of the blade that had entered the complainant's stomach posed a danger to her life, and she could also have died as a result.” The court concluded that administering capsules containing blade pieces amounted to an attempt to murder and constituted cruelty under Section 498A of the IPC. “Feeding capsules containing pieces of a blade to the complainant amounts to an attempt to murder,” the judge held. The court further noted that the accused had allegedly given his wife the capsules over a period of approximately two months and concluded that the prosecution had established the charges under Sections 307 and 498A. However, the court found insufficient evidence to establish the separate allegations that Sapkal had assaulted and abused his wife. It acquitted him of charges under Sections 323 (voluntarily causing hurt) and 504 (intentional insult intended to provoke a breach of peace) of the IPC. During the sentencing hearing, the defence argued that Sapkal was the sole earning member of his family and that his wife was living with him and dependent on him. The court considered these submissions while deciding the punishment. The judge noted the seriousness of the offence but decided against imposing life imprisonment, opting instead for fixed terms of rigorous imprisonment.

news.full_article_text: Watch: Joy and disbelief on Serbian streets as VuÄiÄ concedes election defeat - Published 25 October 2026 Serbia's long-standing leader Aleksandar VuÄiÄ has admitted defeat to the student-led protest movement in snap parliamentary elections. "We still do not have final results... it is clear that we have lost these elections," the right-wing populist leader said as he conceded late on Sunday. Preliminary figures from Serbia's election commission indicated a record high turnout, which commentators had suggested would favour the student movement. Celebrations erupted after VuÄiÄ conceded. VuÄiÄ called the snap elections after two years of protests triggered by the collapse of a train station canopy in the city of Novi Sad, which killed 16 and was seen as emblematic of corruption and negligence. VuÄiÄ said early results made it "clear" that his party had lost VuÄiÄ had spent two terms as president and could not seek a third term, so was leading his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) with the aim of returning to the post of prime minister, which he left in 2017. The Student List's lead candidate Ilija SrdanoviÄ told BBC Serbian: "This will be a free state." He said the anti-corruption movement, which had attracted anti-government voters across Serbia, hoped to "free the country from tyranny". There were celebrations on the streets of the city, with people dancing and chanting "victory", cars honking, and fireworks set off. "Serbia is free," one student told the BBC. "It's a miracle." During a celebration speech, Student List candidate Radomir Saicic said Serbians had shown "no obstacle was greater than their will", Reuters reported. "No force can forever overpower a people who have decided to take their destiny into their own hands," he added. Amid scenes of people dancing in the streets Belgrade, Selena Lebovic said the result was "really fabulous". "We are all crying, and what to say. We couldn't believe that it would be so easy," she told Reuters. An aerial photo shows the size of the celebrations by Students' List supporters at Slavija square in Belgrade VuÄiÄ made his announcement at the headquarters of his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in the capital Belgrade. The centre of Novi Sad - the northern city that triggered the student-led protests - was crowded. "Everything is going to get better now," David VasiÄ, one of those celebrating, told the BBC Serbian. The Student List - which has no obvious leaders and whose members are not used to politics - had attracted anti-government voters across Serbia. It decided to field candidates to the 250-member parliament from across Serbian society including doctors, actors, academics and sports personalities. Ilija SrdanoviÄ, Student List's leading candidate, pictured during celebrations late on Sunday The anti-corruption movement campaigned on a manifesto that included purging officials who broke rules cracking down on protesters, stopping party loyalists from leading public enterprises, and freeing the public broadcaster of political control. VuÄiÄ and the SNS party have repeatedly denied corruption. VuÄiÄ, who backs Serbia's candidacy for the European Union while refusing to impose sanctions on Russia over its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, had pledged to increase pensions and public sector salaries, and investment in state healthcare. Preliminary figures provided by Serbia's election commission suggested a record high turnout, with 64.9% having cast their vote by 18:00 local time (17:00 GMT), two hours before polls were set to close. Earlier in the day, long queues were seen outside polling stations in cities and towns across Serbia. This was also the case outside booths in a number of countries with sizeable Serbian communities - including Slovenia's capital Ljubljana, Germany's Munich, and Los Angeles and Chicago in the US. In France, Serbian voters waited in line in heavy rain in Paris. The election was held amid high tensions across Serbia, with police sealing off streets around the Republic Electoral Commission (RIK) in Belgrade. news.story_lead: Students from Sapphire International School participated in an educational exposure visit to the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). The visit aimed to offer students first-hand insights into India's achievements and ongoing developments in space technology.
news.full_article_text:
### Educational Visit to ISRO

Students from Sapphire International School undertaken an educational visit to the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) to study India's landmark space missions and research initiatives.

### Highlights of the Visit
- **Objective:** To foster scientific curiosity and awareness about satellite technology, space exploration, and rocketry among young students.
- **Focus Areas:** Exposure to Indian space missions, satellite applications, and the technological strides made by ISRO in recent years.
- **Student Engagement:** Interaction with space concepts and gaining awareness regarding opportunities in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) disciplines.

hindi_translation.story_lead: सैफायर इंटरनेशनल स्कूल के छात्रों ने भारतीय अंतरिक्ष अनुसंधान संगठन (ISRO) का शैक्षणिक दौरा किया। इस यात्रा का उद्देश्य छात्रों को भारत की अंतरिक्ष प्रौद्योगिकी और मिशनों के बारे में प्रत्यक्ष जानकारी प्रदान करना था।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### इसरो का शैक्षणिक दौरा

सैफायर इंटरनेशनल स्कूल के छात्रों ने भारत के अंतरिक्ष अभियानों और अनुसंधान पहलों का अध्ययन करने के लिए भारतीय अंतरिक्ष अनुसंधान संगठन (ISRO) का दौरा किया।

### दौरे के मुख्य बिंदु
- **उद्देश्य:** युवा छात्रों के बीच वैज्ञानिक दृष्टिकोण, उपग्रह प्रौद्योगिकी और अंतरिक्ष अन्वेषण के प्रति जागरूकता बढ़ाना।
- **प्रमुख विषय:** भारतीय अंतरिक्ष मिशन, उपग्रह अनुप्रयोग और इसरो द्वारा हासिल की गई तकनीकी प्रगति।
- **छात्र सहभागिता:** अंतरिक्ष अवधारणाओं को समझना और स्टेम (STEM) क्षेत्रों में अवसरों के प्रति जागरूकता बढ़ाना।

यह पहल अंतरिक्ष विज्ञान और प्रौद्योगिकी में युवाओं की रुचि बढ़ाने में सहायक है।
