news.headline: Death toll in Nigeria village raided by gunmen rises to 48, police say
news.story_lead: File image of Nigerian police officers - Published 25 October 2026, 03:20 GMT The death toll from Friday's attack on a remote village in the north-eastern Nigerian state of Taraba has risen to at least 48, police have told the BBC. The police had initially reported 10 deaths after unidentified gunmen on motorcycles raided the village of Binnari, looting shops and setting houses ablaze. More bodies were discovered on Sunday, according to state police spokesperson Victor Mshelizah, who said some of the victims had drowned while trying to escape the attackers while others were killed in nearby bushes.
news.full_article_text: File image of Nigerian police officers - Published 25 October 2026, 03:20 GMT The death toll from Friday's attack on a remote village in the north-eastern Nigerian state of Taraba has risen to at least 48, police have told the BBC. The police had initially reported 10 deaths after unidentified gunmen on motorcycles raided the village of Binnari, looting shops and setting houses ablaze. More bodies were discovered on Sunday, according to state police spokesperson Victor Mshelizah, who said some of the victims had drowned while trying to escape the attackers while others were killed in nearby bushes. Meanwhile, Amnesty International's director for Nigeria said his organisation had confirmed 52 deaths, citing sources on the ground and members of the local community. The attack happened just after midday Muslim prayers, and the rampage went on for up to four hours. State police had initially recovered 10 bodies with gunshot wounds after officers responded to a distress call. The attackers had fled by the time officers arrived - but they continued to patrol the area to restore calm, Taraba's police told the BBC on Saturday. "We were able to disperse the unknown gunmen though there was no casualty on their side and ours because the terrain is difficult and they're used to the terrain," Assistant Superintendent of Police Victor Mshelizah said. Community leader Malam Abubakar Saifullahi told news agency AFP that the attackers had arrived on about 50 motorcycles, two men apiece. "They looted shops and took cash, foodstuffs and other provisions," he said. "They also took motorcycles abandoned by people fleeing the attack." Isiyaku Musa, who survived the attack, told AFP: "People were running in different directions to escape the attack. Nobody knew where it was safe to go." Amnesty's Nigeria director Isa Sanusi has called for an impartial investigation into the killings, accusing the authorities of leaving rural communities "at the mercy of gunmen that are repeatedly commit atrocities with impunity". Parts of north-eastern Nigeria have been affected by years of violence involving jihadist groups and armed gangs, which raid communities, abduct residents and demand ransoms. Similar armed groups operate in the country's north-west and central regions. The latest attack comes as Nigeria prepares for elections next year, with insecurity expected to feature prominently in political debates. - The kidnap gangs, jihadists and separatists wreaking havoc in Nigeria Published 28 November 2025 - 'If you started running, they shot you' - inside Nigeria's growing kidnapping crisis Published 27 August - Inside story of a Nigerian ransom negotiator Published 21 March 2024 Survivors who spoke to AFP said they had counted at least 20 dead. "People were running in different directions to escape the attack," Binnari resident Isiyaku Musa said. "Nobody knew where it was safe to go." Another survivor, Sa'idu Nuhu, said that some people were still missing. Amnesty's Nigeria director, Isa Sanusi, told BBC News on Saturday that the NGO had spoken to some of the bereaved families who said up to 50 people had died. "The initial funeral had 37 people," he said. Sanusi called for an impartial investigation into the killings, accusing the authorities of leaving rural communities "at the mercy of gunmen that are repeatedly commit atrocities with impunity". news.headline: Collegium decisions unanimous, says ex-CJI Chandrachud
news.story_lead: Collegium decisions unanimous, says ex-CJI Chandrachud Former CJI Chandrachud says collegium decisions were unanimous and Kaul endorsed all recommendations, disputing memoir claims of government deference. Former Chief Justice of India (CJI) Dhananjaya Y Chandrachud has responded to former Supreme Court judge Sanjay Kishan Kaul’s account of their interactions over judicial appointments, saying collegium decisions were unanimous and Justice Kaul had endorsed every recommendation. Justice Chandrachud said it would be difficult for him to comment in detail on Kaul’s account in his forthcoming memoir, “Without Fear or Favour”, as he had not yet read the book.
news.full_article_text: Collegium decisions unanimous, says ex-CJI Chandrachud Former CJI Chandrachud says collegium decisions were unanimous and Kaul endorsed all recommendations, disputing memoir claims of government deference. Former Chief Justice of India (CJI) Dhananjaya Y Chandrachud has responded to former Supreme Court judge Sanjay Kishan Kaul’s account of their interactions over judicial appointments, saying collegium decisions were unanimous and Justice Kaul had endorsed every recommendation. Justice Chandrachud said it would be difficult for him to comment in detail on Kaul’s account in his forthcoming memoir, “Without Fear or Favour”, as he had not yet read the book. “Unless I read his observations and understand the context in which they were made, I would not be in a position to offer a detailed response,” he said. Justice Chandrachud, however, added that the collegium’s official records showed that its resolutions, along with the reasons for its recommendations, were made public on the Supreme Court’s website and that the decisions were unanimous, with Justice Kaul endorsing every recommendation. The former CJI further said there was not a single instance of Justice Kaul recording a dissent when the collegium formally proposed candidates to the government for appointment as judges. He said this was an important part of the record to consider while assessing the decision-making process. He also emphasised that collegium decisions were not arrived at abruptly during meetings. “Judges held multiple rounds of informal and formal discussions before names were officially considered and recommendations sent to the government,” he said, adding that Justice Kaul had never walked out of any such meeting. According to Justice Chandrachud, the meetings were conducted in a congenial atmosphere. Justice Kaul, in his memoir, has said the former CJI was “too deferential to the government”. He has argued that discussions with the executive should not amount to seeking the government’s approval before the collegium has formally deliberated on a candidate. One of his most revealing accounts concerns a candidate from a minority faith whose elevation was questioned by the government. According to Justice Kaul, the government first raised the question of whether the Supreme Court needed additional representation from that faith, despite the candidate being from a state under-represented on the court. A further query concerned the caste to which the candidate’s family had belonged before converting to the faith. The former top court judge found the question irrelevant and the reasoning troubling. He says he told Justice Chandrachud that if appointments were to be made on such considerations, the government might as well appoint judges itself. He then shut the file and walked out of the collegium meeting. The meeting was adjourned, and the government eventually relented. Justice Kaul retired as judge of the Supreme Court in December 2023. He was part of the collegium and authored several important judgments since his elevation to the top court on February 17, 2017. Prior to this, he also served as chief justices of the high courts of Punjab & Haryana and Madras. - Supreme Court Collegium

news.headline: At least 2 feared trapped as under-construction building collapses in Delhi's Harsh Vihar
news.story_lead: At least 2 feared trapped as under-construction building collapses in Delhi's Harsh Vihar An under-construction house collapsed in northeast Delhi’s Harsh Vihar. Two are feared trapped under debris. At least two people were feared to be trapped under debris after an under-construction house collapsed in the Milan Garden area of north east Delhi’s Harsh Vihar on Sunday evening.
news.full_article_text: At least 2 feared trapped as under-construction building collapses in Delhi's Harsh Vihar An under-construction house collapsed in northeast Delhi’s Harsh Vihar. Two are feared trapped under debris. At least two people were feared to be trapped under debris after an under-construction house collapsed in the Milan Garden area of north east Delhi’s Harsh Vihar on Sunday evening. A Delhi Fire Service (DFS) official said that call regarding the collapse was received at 6.46pm, following which six fire tenders were pressed into service. Police personnel and rescue teams, including the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), rushed to the spot and began efforts to search for anyone who may have been trapped beneath the rubble. The operation was ongoing at the time of going to print. Among the two people who are reported to be missing are the contractor and his father, said the DFS official. Also read: Amit Shah directs Delhi Police to finish key works within deadlines “When the teams reached the location, they found that the building’s ground floor was an old structure, while the owners were carrying out construction on the first floor,” a senior police officer said. However, the circumstances that led to the collapse were not immediately clear, he said. The owner of the structure has been identified and traced, and legal proceedings have been initiated, the police official said, without giving further details. The incident comes amid a string of building collapses that have shined a spotlight on weak enforcement of building safety laws and lack of proper oversight. On October 7, at least four people died when a building collapsed in New Seemapuri with demolition work in an adjacent building, involving vibrating machines, suspected to have triggered the collapse. Also read: Delhi records October's lowest minimum temperature at 17 degrees Celsius after overnight rain On September 6, a multi-storey boy's hostel collapsed, killing seven people, including five Delhi University students and two labourers. Prior to that, On May 30, a building collapsed in south Delhi’s Saidulajab, killing six people, including five doctors and engineers and one eatery owner. Unauthorised construction was suspected to be the cause in both the incidents.

news.headline: Student movement takes Serbia's Vučić to the wire in neck-and-neck election
news.story_lead: The Student List is Number 3 on Serbia's ballot paper, so the figure seen being hugged by this supporter has become a symbol of the movement's fight for change - Published 24 October 2026 If Sunday's parliamentary elections really are a battle for the heart of Serbia, then who better than a cardiologist to be one of the leading figures in the race. Ilija SrdanoviÄ appears an unlikely opponent for Serbia's long-serving leader, Aleksandar VuÄiÄ, arriving for an interview by motorbike sporting a fluorescent yellow jacket emblazoned with pro-student slogans. He has been selected as top candidate for an opposition movement posing the most serious challenge to VuÄiÄ since the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) entered government in 2012.
news.full_article_text: The Student List is Number 3 on Serbia's ballot paper, so the figure seen being hugged by this supporter has become a symbol of the movement's fight for change - Published 24 October 2026 If Sunday's parliamentary elections really are a battle for the heart of Serbia, then who better than a cardiologist to be one of the leading figures in the race. Ilija SrdanoviÄ appears an unlikely opponent for Serbia's long-serving leader, Aleksandar VuÄiÄ, arriving for an interview by motorbike sporting a fluorescent yellow jacket emblazoned with pro-student slogans. He has been selected as top candidate for an opposition movement posing the most serious challenge to VuÄiÄ since the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) entered government in 2012. The Student List has emerged from almost two years of anti-corruption protests led by young Serbians, outraged by the deaths of 16 people when a railway station's canopy collapsed in Serbia's second city Novi Sad. - What you need to know about Serbia's pivotal election Published 2 days ago Instead of running for office themselves, student-led assemblies at the country's university faculties have chosen 250 candidates to stand in the parliamentary election, with SrdanoviÄ, professor at Novi Sad University, heading the list. "It is absolutely normal to stand with my students to help them in their fair struggle," SrdanoviÄ told the BBC. Ilija SrdanoviÄ tops the Student List's 250 candidates but would not necessarily lead Serbia if they won The Student List is up against a Serbian leader who has served successively as deputy prime minister, prime minister and president since 2012. When he called these snap elections last month , he stood down as president to run again for the role of prime minister. Whatever VuÄiÄ's title, there has never been any doubt that he was the man in charge â an image enthusiastically promoted by Serbia's largely uncritical media. He retains strong support among a significant section of Serbia's population. They view him as a strong leader who stands up for the country's interests. He can also point to significant economic growth over the past decade and numerous improvements in infrastructure. VuÄiÄ has painted the student movement as foreign-backed and seeking to "bring down our state". "Let us always protect and defend it," he told supporters at a final campaign rally. Just like the protest movement from which it developed, the Student List has no hierarchy or nominated leader. This makes it a proposition unlike any other in Serbia's relatively short democratic history. Reliable polls are thin on the ground, but analysts are predicting an extremely tight vote. A reported 150,000 supporters turned out for the final Student List rally in Belgrade's Slavija Square on Thursday night Ilija SrdanoviÄ may head the list of candidates â but he is not the movement's leader and would not necessarily be first choice prime minister if they won. SrdanoviÄ insists that the Student List has a clear vision: "We offer to our citizens the core values of civilised society, which this previous regime has taken away from our citizens for the last time." The other candidates on the Student List range from academics to athletes â and economists to engineers. None of them has a political background. But the students who selected them believe that is a strength, rather than a weakness. "We've gathered people who are actually the best in their fields, and we really think that they are competent enough to rule the country," says Aleksandra, a student at Novi Sad University who only wants to give her first name. "All of them are gathered around the same vision of a country where the freedom of speech is ruling, where you can walk to your home in the middle of the night and you will not be beaten up by some hooligans," she adds. The Student List and its supporters say that Aleksandar VuÄiÄ and the SNS dominate state institutions and media coverage. At the last parliamentary election in 2023, the International Election Observation Mission noted "overwhelming ruling party advantage" due to "bias in the media" and "misuse of public office and resources". The BBC approached leading figures in the SNS for an interview but was not offered a response. VuÄiÄ continues to command strong support among sections of Serbia's population For the past 18 months, there has also been a full-time, pro-SNS camp in the small park between the National Assembly and the Presidency building in the centre of Belgrade. Its residents have repeatedly attacked journalists and made the park a no-go zone for local people. VuÄiÄ has called the camp "a symbol of resistance" against those who "cannot stand different opinions". But his major challenge remains what happened outside Novi Sad railway station two years ago. The station's renovation was a key part of his signature infrastructure project â the high-speed line linking Belgrade and Budapest. So it has been difficult for VuÄiÄ to distance himself from the disaster. Aleksandar VuÄiÄ stepped down as president last month with the aim of returning to the post of prime minister Protests followed, with participants accusing the authorities of corruption and having "blood on their hands". "This is a problem for the government," says Magda Anastasijevic, the Eastern Europe analyst for the conflict monitor, ACLED. "VuÄiÄ has survived this in the past, he was always able to find a scapegoat and blame whatever problems on them. This was not the case for the canopy." On the diplomatic front, he has performed a delicate balancing act. Membership talks with the EU continue, albeit fitfully, even as Serbia retains close ties with Russia and China â both countries that refuse to recognise Kosovo's unilateral declaration of independence from Serbia. VuÄiÄ has warned those links could be severed if the Student List took power. "When you ask them: will you impose sanctions on Russia? Silence, umming and ah-ing, but no answer," he told the audience at a pre-election rally. "You know what the Chinese think, you've heard what Vladimir Putin said. So you decide. Think about who has our best interests at heart." The final rallies of the campaign saw the SNS stage an event at Belgrade Arena, with Aleksandar VuÄiÄ as the only speaker. But on the other side of the Sava River, the Student List attracted a reported 150,000 people in Slavija Square to listen to a mixture of students and candidates. The contrasting visions were clear to see: the strong, sole leader â or a collective approach. Now Serbia's electorate must decide which they prefer. Related topics

### High Turnout Recorded in Serbian Early Elections

Serbia held snap parliamentary elections with preliminary official figures showing a turnout of 64.9% by 18:00 local time (17:00 GMT), two hours prior to the closure of polls across 8,210 voting booths. High turnout levels were observed both domestically and at overseas voting locations in cities like Paris, Munich, Ljubljana, Chicago, and Los Angeles.

### Key Parties and Electoral Dynamics

- **Serbian Progressive Party (SNS)**: Headed by 56-year-old Aleksandar Vučić, who has maintained political dominance since 2012. Having served two presidential terms, Vučić is campaigning to return to the position of Prime Minister. The SNS occupies position number one on the ballot paper.
- **Student List**: Appearing as number three on the ballot, this civic opposition movement is led by Novi Sad University professor Ilija Srdanović. Its list of 250 parliamentary candidates includes educators, medical professionals, actors, and athletes chosen by university assemblies rather than conventional politicians.
- **Protest Origins**: Public demonstrations intensified following a 2024 canopy collapse at a railway station in Novi Sad, which caused 16 fatalities and became a symbol of administrative corruption and infrastructure neglect.

### Electoral Infrastructure and Monitoring Allegations

With 6.45 million registered voters out of a total population of 6.53 million, observers highlighted potential register inaccuracies. Serbian citizens residing in Kosovo and dual citizens in Bosnia also retained voting rights. To prevent potential electoral manipulation, the Student List deployed at least two monitors to every voting station.

Independent monitoring organization CRTA noted numerous irregularities and localized violent incidents. Reports emerged from Niš regarding alleged 'chain voting'—a fraudulent practice where ballot papers are pre-marked prior to entering polling booths.
news.background_context: The snap elections follow two years of student-led anti-corruption protests triggered by the November 2024 train station roof collapse in Novi Sad, which killed 16 people. The tragedy fueled widespread public discontent over official negligence and regulatory oversights.
bullet_points: Preliminary voter turnout reached 64.9% by 18:00 local time in Serbia's early parliamentary elections.
The early elections follow two years of civic demonstrations triggered by a 2024 infrastructure collapse in Novi Sad that killed 16 people.
President Aleksandar Vučić and his ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) seek to retain power, with Vučić contesting for the Prime Minister role.
The main opposition force, 'Student List', fields 250 non-traditional candidates selected through university assemblies.
Voting was conducted across 8,210 polling booths in Serbia as well as polling stations abroad in France, Germany, Slovenia, and the USA.
Serbia's voter roll comprises 6.45 million individuals out of a overall national population of 6.53 million.
Independent election observer CRTA reported irregularities and instances of violence, alongside social media reports of illegal 'chain voting' in Niš.

Electorate Size: 6.45 million registered voters out of 6.53 million residents

exam_relevance: Prelims: Geographical knowledge of the Balkan region, terms related to electoral processes (e.g., 'chain voting').
Mains: Comparative governance, civil society movements, role of electoral watchdogs, and political stability in Eastern Europe.
news.upsc_analysis: The 2026 Serbian snap elections demonstrate the ability of grassroots civic movements to transition from anti-corruption protests to formal parliamentary candidates. The event underscores the critical role played by civil society monitoring in safeguarding democratic procedures during high-stakes elections.
causes: Public outrage over public corruption and infrastructure negligence stemming from the 2024 Novi Sad train station canopy collapse that killed 16 people.
Demands by student groups to halt political interference in state enterprises and public broadcasting.
impacts: High voter engagement and political mobilization across domestic and international polling centers.
Potential political realignment or extended post-election instability if results are disputed by major political blocs.
challenges: Allegations of electoral fraud, including pre-marked ballots and 'chain voting' practices.
Concerns regarding electoral roll inflation, with registered voters (6.45 million) closely approaching the official population (6.53 million).
Lack of formal legislative experience among student-nominated opposition candidates.
government_steps: Deployment of police forces around critical state infrastructure, including the Republic Electoral Commission (RIK) in Belgrade.
Facilitation of voting setups across overseas diplomatic bases.
constitutional_or_policy_link: Electoral oversight mechanisms and candidate selection procedures in parliamentary systems.
Constitutional presidential term limits influencing political leadership transitions.
way_forward: Comprehensive verification of vote tallies by independent election observation bodies.
Establishing transparent post-election dialogues to ensure democratic stability regardless of outcome.
news.mains_notes: Grassroots Political Movements in Democracies: The Serbian elections offer an example of non-party civic assemblies nominating professional experts (academics, doctors, actors) to challenge political incumbents on anti-corruption and public oversight mandates.
mains_questions: Discuss how student-led movements can influence policy accountability and political structures in modern parliamentary democracies.
Examine the key administrative and procedural challenges associated with maintaining electoral integrity during contested elections.
news.takeaway: Serbia's snap parliamentary elections saw high voter participation driven by a university student-led movement contesting the prolonged rule of the Serbian Progressive Party.
prelims_facts: Belgrade is the capital city of Serbia.
'Chain voting' refers to an illicit electoral practice where pre-filled ballot papers are introduced into polling stations from the outside.
Serbia's snap elections involved 8,210 polling stations serving an electorate of 6.45 million people.

hindi_translation.headline: छात्र नेतृत्व वाले विपक्ष की चुनौती के बीच सर्बिया में मध्यावधि चुनाव में भारी मतदान
hindi_translation.story_lead: सर्बिया में मध्यावधि संसदीय चुनाव आयोजित किए गए, जिसमें देर शाम तक लगभग 65% मतदान दर्ज किया गया। यह मध्यावधि चुनाव राष्ट्रपति अलेक्जेंडर वुचिच के लंबे शासन को चुनौती देने वाले छात्र-नेतृत्व वाले भ्रष्टाचार विरोधी आंदोलन के बाद हुआ है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### सर्बियाई मध्यावधि चुनावों में भारी मतदान

सर्बिया में मध्यावधि संसदीय चुनाव आयोजित हुए, जिसमें प्रारंभिक आधिकारिक आंकड़ों के अनुसार 8,210 मतदान केंद्रों पर स्थानीय समयानुसार 18:00 बजे तक 64.9% मतदान हुआ। पेरिस, म्यूनिख, ल्युब्लियाना, शिकागो और लॉस एंजिल्स जैसे शहरों में घरेलू और विदेशी दोनों स्तरों पर उच्च भागीदारी देखी गई।

### प्रमुख दल और चुनावी गतिशीलता

- **सर्बियाई प्रोग्रेसिव पार्टी (SNS)**: 56 वर्षीय अलेक्जेंडर वुचिच के नेतृत्व वाली पार्टी, जो 2012 से सत्ता में है। दो राष्ट्रपति कार्यकाल पूरा करने के बाद, वुचिच प्रधानमंत्री पद पर लौटने के लिए चुनाव लड़ रहे हैं। मतपत्र पर SNS पहले स्थान पर है।
- **स्टूडेंट लिस्ट**: मतपत्र पर तीसरे स्थान पर मौजूद इस नागरिक विपक्षी आंदोलन का नेतृत्व नोवी साद विश्वविद्यालय के प्रोफेसर इलिजा सरडानोविच कर रहे हैं। इनके 250 उम्मीदवारों की सूची में पारंपरिक राजनेताओं के बजाय संकाय सभाओं द्वारा चुने गए शिक्षक, डॉक्टर, अभिनेता और खिलाड़ी शामिल हैं।
- **विरोध का कारण**: नोवी साद में एक रेलवे स्टेशन की छत गिरने से 16 लोगों की मौत के बाद जनता का गुस्सा भड़क उठा, जो प्रशासनिक भ्रष्टाचार और लापरवाही का प्रतीक बन गया।

### चुनावी ढांचा और निगरानी के आरोप

6.53 मिलियन की कुल जनसंख्या में से 6.45 मिलियन पंजीकृत मतदाता होने के कारण, पर्यवेक्षकों ने मतदाता सूची की विश्वसनीयता पर चिंता व्यक्त की। छात्र सूची ने चुनावी धांधली रोकने के लिए प्रत्येक मतदान केंद्र पर कम से कम दो पर्यवेक्षक तैनात किए।

स्वतंत्र निगरानी संगठन CRTA ने कई अनियमितताओं और हिंसक घटनाओं की सूचना दी। नीश (Niş) शहर से 'चेन वोटिंग' (पूर्व-चिह्नित मतपत्रों का अवैध उपयोग) के आरोप सामने आए।
hindi_translation.background_context: मध्यावधि चुनाव नोवी साद में नवंबर 2024 में ट्रेन स्टेशन की छत ढहने से हुई 16 मौतों के बाद शुरू हुए दो साल के छात्र विरोध प्रदर्शनों का परिणाम हैं।
bullet_points: सर्बिया के मध्यावधि संसदीय चुनावों में स्थानीय समयानुसार 18:00 बजे तक 64.9% मतदान दर्ज किया गया।
यह चुनाव 2024 में नोवी साद बुनियादी ढांचा हादसे के बाद शुरू हुए दो साल के छात्र विरोध प्रदर्शनों के बाद हुआ है।
राष्ट्रपति अलेक्जेंडर वुचिच और उनकी सत्तारूढ़ पार्टी (SNS) सत्ता बनाए रखने की कोशिश कर रहे हैं।
विपक्षी 'स्टूडेंट लिस्ट' ने विश्वविद्यालय सभाओं द्वारा चुने गए 250 गैर-पारंपरिक उम्मीदवारों को मैदान में उतारा है।
मतदान सर्बिया के 8,210 मतदान केंद्रों के साथ-साथ फ्रांस, जर्मनी, स्लोवेनिया और अमेरिका में भी आयोजित किया गया।
सर्बिया की 6.53 मिलियन आबादी में से पंजीकृत मतदाताओं की संख्या 6.45 मिलियन है।
स्वतंत्र चुनाव पर्यवेक्षक CRTA ने मतदान केंद्रों के बाहर अनियमितताओं और हिंसक घटनाओं की सूचना दी।
key_facts: मतदान प्रतिशत: 18:00 बजे तक 64.9%
मतदाता संख्या: 6.53 मिलियन जनसंख्या में से 6.45 मिलियन पंजीकृत मतदाता
मतदान केंद्र: देश भर में 8,210 केंद्र
मुख्य विपक्षी उम्मीदवार: प्रोफेसर इलिजा सरडानोविच
मतपत्र स्थिति: SNS (#1), स्टूडेंट लिस्ट (#3)

quiz.question: In the context of electoral processes, what does the term 'chain voting' refer to?
options: A) Voting sequentially at multiple polling stations using different legal identity cards
B) An illegal practice where pre-marked ballots are smuggled into polling stations and blank ballots removed
C) A system allowing overseas citizens to cast votes across consecutive operational days
D) Mandatory voting requirements enforced by electoral management bodies during runoff elections
quiz.correct_answer: B) An illegal practice where pre-marked ballots are smuggled into polling stations and blank ballots removed
quiz.explanation: Chain voting is an illegal electoral fraud technique where voters are given pre-marked ballot papers prior to entering the voting booth, subsequently bringing their official blank ballot paper back out to perpetrators.
